title: Peering ghost-route rollback and observability hardening for dedicated tenant egress
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Several Dedicated customers reported transient cross-tenant DNS resolution and intermittent connections to the wrong egress path shortly after GPU pool scale events and peering reconverges. This ticket implements a safe rollback and reconciliation mechanism for 'ghost' peering routes, hardens observability to detect route-programming divergence earlier, and ships a guarded production fix to prevent future regressions.
impact_summary: Customer-facing incidents observed across 3 enterprise Dedicated tenants (high traffic inference workloads). Symptoms: DNS lookups resolving private hostnames from other tenants and sporadic outbound flows using stale overlay routes during peering resyncs. Impact: increased error rates for affected tenants, data isolation concern escalated to SRE and sales for two accounts; severity: Sev2 for customer-facing reliability, regulatory risk noted.
root_cause: Race in peering control-plane reconciliation combined with delayed dataplane route garbage collection. After peering switchover (control-plane reparenting or EVPN sync), some overlay VNIs had stale route entries on a subset of nodes. When ephemeral SNAT port reuse and L2 learning updates occurred concurrently, host-level resolver caches and Nat mappings could transiently point to the wrong tenant egress. The primary contributor was missing a deterministic backstop during partial reconciliations: no step enforced a canonical final state before garbage-collecting old routes.
mitigation:
Immediate mitigations deployed (Feb 12):
- Fast rollback: introduced a temporary backstop rule that pins tenant egress to last-known-good overlay next-hop while full reconciliation completes. This prevents immediate drift during ephemeral failures.
- Cache eviction: proactively invalidated local resolver/KV caches on nodes that received peering updates to avoid stale DNS answers.
- Rate-limited peering resync window: slowed control-plane churn during high-scale operations.
These mitigations reduced incident recurrence and lowered customer error rates to baseline within 3 hours for affected accounts.
proposed_fix:
1) Reconciliation backstop: implement a two-phase peering reconcile that first stages candidate route changes, performs dataplane reconcile checks, and only then switches active egress pointers atomically (circuit-breaker semantics).
2) Deterministic GC: change route garbage collector to require consensus across N/2+1 controllers before deleting last-known-host routes.
3) Observability: add a route-divergence metric and alert (route-programmed != route-intended) with per-tenant granularity; expose suspect nodes in Console.
4) E2E regression tests: synthetic scale-up/scale-down with peering flaps in CI and dedicated chaos job in staging.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 - Canary (2 nodes in staging, Mar 09): run reconcile with passive monitoring.
Phase 1 - Small production canary (10% rings for non-critical tenants, Mar 12): enable backstop and divergence alerting.
Phase 2 - Broad rollout (Mar 18): enable two-phase reconcile on all Dedicated clusters after soak.
Rollback plan: configuration flag to disable two-phase reconcile and re-enable previous behavior; also keep emergency backstop policy for 72 hours after rollback.
verification_plan:
- Automated end-to-end test that validates no cross-tenant DNS/egress mapping during peering resync
- Dashboards: tenant-route-divergence, per-node resolver-stale-count
- Post-deploy smoke: run customer-sim job for 6 hours and monitor 99th pct latency and error-rate for DNS and egress flows
- Manual audit: sampling of netstat/conntrack and Geneve VNI tables on canary nodes
